never(call): thread.run() -- runs synchronously on the caller's thread; call thread.start() to actually run it concurrently
x = x; as a bare statement, both sides the exact same plain variable name
never(statement): x = x; -- changes nothing; likely meant this.x = x; to set the field from a same-named parameter
Math.abs() of a hashCode() or a random int
never(call): Math.abs(x.hashCode()) | Math.abs(random.nextInt()) -- both can still be Integer.MIN_VALUE, which stays negative under Math.abs()
Integer division cast to double after the fact
double d = 7 / 2; and other assignments dividing two plain integer literals
never(assign): double d = intLiteral / intLiteral; -- divides as integers, truncating, before widening; make an operand a double first
a static (with or without final) field typed SimpleDateFormat, DateFormat, MessageFormat, DecimalFormat or Calendar

never(declare): static SimpleDateFormat|DateFormat|MessageFormat|DecimalFormat|Calendar field -- these mutate on every call and are not thread-safe; use an instance field, a ThreadLocal, or DateTimeFormatter
Unsynchronized Access to Shared Data in a Multithreaded Context
Double-checked locking on a non-volatile field
the null/synchronized/null-again/assign idiom on a field never declared volatile
never(pattern): if (x == null) { synchronized (...) { if (x == null) { x = ...; } } } unless x is volatile -- otherwise a thread can see a non-null, half-constructed x
synchronized on a string literal, new Object(), getClass() or a boxed constant
synchronized("a literal"); synchronized(new Object()); synchronized(getClass()); synchronized(Boolean.TRUE)
never(lock): synchronized("literal"|new Object()|getClass()|Boolean.TRUE|Integer.valueOf(n)) -- none of these is a lock exclusive to this critical section; use a private final Object field
synchronized (lock) { } with nothing but whitespace or a comment inside
never(block): synchronized (lock) { } -- pays for the lock and forces a happens-before edge that protects nothing; fill it in or remove it
wait() not called inside a loop
Object.wait()/x.wait() reached with no enclosing while or for loop
never(call): x.wait() outside a while/for loop -- spurious wakeups and races between notify() and resuming both need the condition rechecked
Thread.sleep() called while holding a lock
Thread.sleep(...) reached from inside a synchronized(...) { } block
never(call): Thread.sleep(...) inside a synchronized block -- blocks every other thread waiting on that lock for the whole sleep; move it outside
a bare notify() call, or this.notify()
never(call): notify() | this.notify() -- wakes an arbitrary single waiter, which can be the wrong one; use notifyAll()
Closeable or executor opened without try-with-resources or a finally close
a stream, reader, writer, connection, statement, socket, or ExecutorService assigned to a local outside a `try (` header, with no close()/shutdown() call anywhere later in the method

never(declare): a local FileInputStream|FileOutputStream|FileReader|FileWriter|BufferedReader|RandomAccessFile|ZipFile|JarFile|Socket|ServerSocket|Files.newInputStream|DriverManager.getConnection|dataSource.getConnection|conn.createStatement|conn.prepareStatement|Executors.newFixedThreadPool outside a try-with-resources header with no close()/shutdown() in a finally -- use try-with-resources
Missing Release of Resource after Effective Lifetime
a class declaring `void finalize()`, at any visibility
never(override): protected void finalize() -- use try-with-resources, close()/shutdown(), or java.lang.ref.Cleaner
System.gc(), Runtime.getRuntime().gc(), or System.runFinalization() called from application code
never(call): System.gc()|Runtime.getRuntime().gc()|System.runFinalization() -- let the collector decide when to run
System.exit() called outside a main method
System.exit/Runtime.exit/Runtime.halt in a file that declares no `static void main(`
never(call): System.exit(...)|Runtime.getRuntime().exit(...)|Runtime.getRuntime().halt(...) outside static void main(...) -- throw or return an error instead
J2EE Bad Practices: Use of System.exit()
never(call): System.runFinalizersOnExit(...)|Runtime.getRuntime().runFinalizersOnExit(...) -- there is no safe replacement, remove the call
a catch block with no statements and no comment inside it
never(catch): an exception with an empty block and no comment -- handle it, log it with context, or rethrow it
`catch (Throwable ...)` or `catch (Error ...)`, alone or in a multi-catch
never(catch): Throwable|Error directly -- catch the specific exception types this code can recover from
Declaration of Catch for Generic Exception
`catch (NullPointerException e)`, alone or in a multi-catch
never(catch): NullPointerException -- check for null explicitly instead of catching it
Use of NullPointerException Catch to Detect NULL Pointer Dereference
return or throw inside a finally block
a `return` or `throw` statement at the finally block's own top level
never(place): return|throw directly inside a finally block -- it silently replaces the exception the try was propagating
`throw new Exception(...)`, `new RuntimeException(...)`, `new Throwable(...)`, or `new Error(...)`
never(throw): new Exception(...)|new RuntimeException(...)|new Throwable(...)|new Error(...) -- define and throw a specific exception type
Declaration of Throws for Generic Exception
Caught exception not passed as the new exception's cause
`throw new Y(...)` inside a catch block where none of the constructor arguments is the caught variable itself (e.g. `throw new Y(e.getMessage())` or `throw new Y("message")`)
never(throw): new X(...) inside a catch block without passing the caught exception as an argument -- pass it as the cause
Boxed primitive or String constructed with new
never(construct): new Integer(...)|new Long(...)|new Short(...)|new Byte(...)|new Double(...)|new Float(...)|new Boolean(...)|new Character(...)|new String(...) -- use valueOf(...) or a literal
String concatenated with '+' inside a loop
`name += ...` or `name = name + ...` on a String local declared in the same method, inside a for/while/do loop body
never(concatenate): a String local with += or `x = x + ...` inside a for/while/do loop -- build it with a StringBuilder outside the loop instead
Map.keySet() iterated then get() called for every key
a `for (K k : map.keySet())` loop whose body calls `map.get(k)` on that same map and key
never(iterate): for (K k : map.keySet()) { ... map.get(k) ... } -- iterate map.entrySet() and read the value from the entry
size()/length() compared to zero instead of isEmpty()
`.size() == 0`/`> 0`/`!= 0` on a List/Set/Map/Collection/Queue/Deque local declared in this method; `.length() == 0`/`> 0`/`!= 0` on a String local declared in this method
never(compare): collection.size() == 0|> 0|!= 0, or string.length() == 0|> 0|!= 0 -- use isEmpty()/!isEmpty() instead
never(construct): new Vector(...)|new Hashtable(...)|new Stack(...) -- use ArrayList/HashMap/ArrayDeque, or java.util.concurrent for real thread-sharing
`import java.lang.String;`, `import java.lang.*;`; a second `import` of the same name; a type imported from this file's own package
never(import): a java.lang type, a type from this file's own package, or the same import twice
System.out.println/print or System.err.println/print in a production class with no `static void main(`
never(call): System.out.print*/System.err.print* outside tests and outside a main() class -- use a logger
`x == true`, `x == false`, `x != true`, `x != false`, in either operand order
never(compare): expr == true|false|expr != true|false -- use the expression itself, negated with ! if needed
`if (cond);`, `for (...);`, `while (cond);` on one line, with nothing or only whitespace between `)` and `;`
never(write): if (...); / for (...); / while (...); -- an empty statement where a block was meant
`private static final String tableName = ...;`, `static final int maxRetries = 3;`
Multiple variables declared in one statement
`int a, b;`, `String first, last;`, `double x = 0, y = 0;`
never(declare): int a, b; -- one variable declaration per statement
Long literal with lowercase l suffix
never(write): a long literal suffixed with lowercase l -- use uppercase L
`String args[]`, `public static void main(String argv[])`, `int matrix[][]`
never(declare): Type name[] -- write Type[] name instead
an @Test/@ParameterizedTest/@RepeatedTest method whose body calls nothing from JUnit, AssertJ, Hamcrest, Mockito, MockMvc or StepVerifier that checks a value
never(write): @Test method with no assertThat/assertEquals/verify/assertThrows/... call and no @Test(expected=...)
`Thread.sleep(500)` anywhere in a test class's body
never(call): Thread.sleep(...) in a test -- use Awaitility or an explicit wait instead
never(write): @Disabled or @Ignore with no reason string -- always @Disabled("why")
assertTrue used for an equality check
never(call): assertTrue(a.equals(b)) / assertTrue(a == b) -- use assertEquals(a, b)
assertFalse used for an equals() check
assertEquals literal in the actual-value position
never(call): assertEquals(actual, 42) -- assertEquals(expected, actual) takes the expected value first
